component.name: Collins
component.summary: Manage and resume your AI coding agent sessions

description.p: A native desktop companion for the Claude Code CLI. Browse every session on your machine in a sidebar grouped by project, give sessions custom names, star favorites, and resume any of them in embedded terminal tabs.

ul.li: Sessions grouped by project with favorites, search, and live updates
Tabbed embedded terminals resuming sessions in their project directory
Attention indicators when a background session produces output
Session details: message counts, models, token usage
Bulk selection for opening, starring, hiding, or trashing sessions

description.p: Unofficial community tool — not affiliated with or endorsed by Anthropic. The agents' own session data is never modified.
Collins is a fork of agent-session-manager by Máté Molnár.

screenshot.caption: Sessions grouped by project in the sidebar, with one resumed in an embedded terminal

description.p: In-app notifications, an effort picker, and Collins on Fedora.

ul.li: Install from the episode6/stable COPR on Fedora and RHEL 10
A session that wants you shows a card in the window with a sound; a header bell opens the notification history, with a choice of sounds and a light/dark card pin
Collins checks once a day for a newer release and says so
New sessions open onto a new-chat screen with model and effort pickers; unsent screens are kept as drafts
A Token use preferences group and a first-launch dialog disclose everything that runs Claude on your behalf; an expired login repairs itself
Paste images into the composer; big drafts survive the round trip
A narrow editor column shows the file tree and the file one at a time
The status icon shows when agents are working; PR drafts offer mark-ready-and-merge

description.p: Available from the episode6 Ubuntu PPA and from PyPI, with every keyboard shortcut rebindable.

ul.li: Install with ppa:episode6/stable on Ubuntu 24.04 and 26.04, or pipx install collins
Installs alongside agent-session-manager instead of clashing with it
Keyboard Bindings dialog: every shortcut is rebindable; Ctrl+K is the quick switcher
Close can hide the window and keep sessions running; the status icon brings it back
Spawned sessions inherit the caller's model and permission mode; Generate Icon picks its model per run
The model list is cached for a day and grouped by family
PR pages render changed images, open wider when there is room, and follow running checks live
The composer opens on typing, never loses a draft, and its spell-check menu aims at the clicked word
Ctrl+click finishes a wrapped link from the transcript; preferences regrouped into ten groups
New name, command (collins), and app id (com.episode6.Collins)
Config moves to ~/.config/collins, migrated automatically
Interactive prompt cards over the terminal
Advanced new-session flags: model, permission mode, extra directories, continue
Permanent delete; folder path in the sidebar
New generic agent icon and banner
UI translations: Hungarian, German, Spanish, French
Selectable terminal color themes
Multiple windows
Interrupted-session badge
AUR and Ubuntu PPA packages
Waiting badge for sessions where Claude asked a question
Export a session transcript as Markdown
Now on PyPI: pipx install agent-session-manager-gtk
Quick switcher (Ctrl+Shift+K) to jump to any session
New Session remembers your last folder; resizable sidebar
Read-only MCP servers browser
Drag to reorder tabs
Transcript peek: recent messages in the session details
Desktop notifications when a background session goes idle
MCP servers and per-session MCP usage in the details dialog
Online documentation site
Set a per-tab emoji prefix from the tab menu
Shift+Enter inserts a newline in Claude's prompt
Clearer active-tab styling and a close-all-tabs button

description.p: Search, graceful close, and sidebar polish.

ul.li: Find bar inside each terminal tab (Ctrl+Shift+G)
Closing a tab asks Claude to exit cleanly (/exit) in the background
Copy session ID from the tab menu
Groups collapsed by default; session rows styled as cards
Renameable tabs and per-tab status dots
Toggleable sidebar with a status footer
Confirmation before closing a tab with a running command
Installable .deb package
